Welcome to the TFC Forgery Companion

Everything you need for TerraFirmaCraft forging in one offline page: look up any of the 774 anvil recipes with its shortest step order and exact target, solve alloy mixes down to the millibucket, or browse every rock type and the ores that spawn in it. Pick a section below to get started.

How to use: type your world seed in the box above — every row recomputes instantly. Seeds you type are remembered in this browser: click the seed box again to re-pick any earlier one, and press ☆ Set default to make a seed load automatically the next time you open the page (a fresh browser starts at 0). The exact target work value for each recipe is printed in gold under the step count (it appears on the anvil GUI at 13 + work px from the left of the progress bar). Press the buttons in the shown order; the last three chips (highlighted gold) are the ones the recipe rules actually inspect.
Made from lists the materials the recipe accepts — tags usually allow several interchangeable items. One is drawn (with its chain, drawn left → right down to the base: ingot, double ingot, double sheet, nugget… — anything no anvil recipe produces); click the +N chip next to it to see the remaining options in a menu. Materials that share a display name (for example the aluminium/aluminum spellings) are shown once, keeping the better sprite. The icon on the right is the product.
Mods: the button next to the search box ticks which of the 38 recipe sources are shown (all on by default = the full HTFC4 pack; your choice is remembered). Where the pack overrides a mod's own recipe file, the pack version is the one used — that is also what happens in-game.
Favorites: click the star next to a recipe to keep it. Your picks are saved in this browser and reappear after a reload; pick View: favorites only to see just those, or use Clear all favorites to start over.
Verified: target values were cross-checked against a Java reimplementation of Minecraft's Xoroshiro128PlusPlus + forkPositional().fromHashOf(recipeId).nextInt(74) over 18,104 (seed, recipe) pairs with zero mismatches; every step order was replayed in-game rules and matches TFC's own calculateOptimalStepsToTarget exactly. Because every sequence is the shortest possible one, recipes with apply_forging_bonus come out Perfectly Forged every time.
Item sprites, material sprites and the forge-step button icons are the actual in-game textures, cut straight out of the TFC / mod jars.
Alloy
How to use: pick an alloy, then type a whole number of mB into any component's box to lock it (press ✕ or clear the box to unlock). With nothing locked, each row shows how much of that metal you need for 1 ingot (100 mB). Lock one component and the page solves the mix for you: every other component gets its possible mB range and the total gets a range too. Lock them all and it reports the exact total, the ingot equivalent, and each component's real percentage with a ✓/✗ against the recipe window.
Ranges are exact: every combination inside them satisfies min · total ≤ component ≤ max · total for all metals at once (the same rule the game checks when you pour the fluids), and no value outside them can. Red means the locks you typed cannot form a valid alloy.
Values are millibuckets of fluid — 100 mB = 1 ingot. The pack's own recipes are used, so where HTFC4 overrides TFC (bismuth bronze, stainless steel, the three andesite alloys) you get the pack numbers.
Production chains: every step shows the machine, what goes in, what comes out and the recipe's parameters — anvil tier and hit order, temperature, duration, fluid amounts. A PACK badge marks a step the HTFC4 pack overrides. Alternates list other mods' routes to the same product; a step with Open in calculator jumps back to the crucible view with that alloy preselected, and Related chains below jump between chains. These are production routes, not crucible alloys — the crucible list above still holds the pourable recipes.
No rocks or ores match.
How to read this: each card is one rock type (grouped into the four geology families from TFC's field guide); under it sit every ore or deposit that can spawn in that rock, with its spawn height range in gold. surface marks ores that also appear in surface soil discs on the ocean floor (tin, copper, gold, silver), and negative numbers are below sea level.
Only veins that are actually switched on in this pack are listed — the enabled set is taken from the game's in_biome/veins.json tags across TFC, Artisanal, Firmalife and tfc_ie_addon, plus HTFC4's own additions. Dikes, gravel, kaolin clay and geodes are left out (they place plain rock, clay or gems rather than mineable ore veins), and so are ores from unrelated mods. Height ranges from several veins of the same ore in the same rock are merged.
